subject: Post-demo: performance deep-dive and lab test plan (HyperAPI)
body:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Kaur <a.kaur@hyperapi.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: performance deep-dive and lab test plan (HyperAPI)

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion and some clear signal on where HyperAPI is seeing production pain. Quick recap + proposed next tests so we can align on a head-to-head A/B that focuses on the things you care about (p95/p99 and tokens/sec under realistic seq distributions).

Recap of constraints you called out:
- Two primary workloads: short chat (avg 30–80 tokens) and long-document completion (avg 1.5k–4k tokens).
- Tight p95 SLO target for interactive flows (~200–300ms target).
- Some traffic will have KV cache hits (conversation state) and some cold-starts.
- Regulatory: traces redacted (PII), but you can share anonymized traces — thanks for offering.

Proposed A/B lab matrix (initial):
1) Baseline (no KV cache, single request routing): Redwood default batching disabled to emulate a cold path. Measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec, 95th percentile throughput.
2) Production mimic (KV caching enabled, continuous batching heuristics): same request stream but with session affinity to exercise KV reuse.
3) Quantized / small-batch variant: run with int8 quantized model to estimate cost/latency tradeoff (if you want cost signal).

Metrics to capture (we'll synthesize if you can't share traces):
- latency: p50, p95, p99 per payload type and per seq-length bucket
- tokens/sec and tokens-per-GPU-second (end-to-end)
- batch size distribution and tail queue time
- cache hit ratio and cache-relative latency delta
- error rate / truncations / timeouts

Owners & timeline:
- Redwood infra: Marissa (lab run orchestration, scripts, aggregator dashboards) — action: create runbook and trace schema by Thu 10/22.
- Redwood runtime: Rishi (ensure KV/cache settings and model pins for repeatable runs).
- HyperAPI: Anita (provide anonymized traces + run mirror tests if you want to run from your side).

Attachments: demo trace we captured (anonymized) and a Mutual Action Plan template (stub attached).

Next steps (concrete):
- Anita: send anonymized trace + confirmation which model variant HyperAPI wants compared (their current production model + any custom prompt layers) by EOD 10/21.
- Marissa: publish runbook + test harness link (Drive) by 10/22.
- Rishi/infra: create a small canary and run 1 short-chat and 1 long-doc A/B by 10/26; summary readout 10/27.

If HyperAPI agrees we can also include a hyperscaler baseline (we suggested two comparator configs to mirror what you saw in prod). That will help isolate where queuing vs kernel selection is contributing to p95/p99.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Rishi to take on the lab setup.

--
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
loganw@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0142

From: Anita Kaur <a.kaur@hyperapi.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up

Thanks Logan — good session. Two clarifying points from our side before we ship traces:
1) Our traces include session IDs and timestamps; we will strip user identifiers but want to keep sequence markers so you can compute cache hit ratios. Is that OK?
2) We run a proprietary preprocessor that fuses short-history tokens into a single context window. For a fair head-to-head, should we give you preprocessed outputs or raw token streams?

Also, on the hyperscaler baseline: we use their managed endpoint for the majority of short-chat traffic and a self-hosted variant for large docs. If you can mirror both modes (managed vs self-hosted), that would be ideal.

Happy to share a 15–30 min window tomorrow to walk a sample trace.

Best,
Anita
Principal Product Manager, Performance
HyperAPI Inc.
a.kaur@hyperapi.com | +1 617-555-0199


On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

Logan / Anita — thanks for the notes. Small clarifications and the test plan detail from our side below.

Test harness details (what Redwood will run unless HyperAPI prefers to run and share results):
- Runner: k6 + custom bench harness that replays anonymized traces at wall-clock arrival times.
- Model pin: we'll pin to the exact open model hash you provide (and a Redwood-verified quantized variant for the quant probe).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16 concurrent worker clients to capture saturation behavior.
- Target: maintain 95% availability during runs; stop if error rate >1.5% over 5m window.

Buckets for reporting:
- short-chat: < 100 tokens
- medium: 100–1024 tokens
- long-doc: > 1024 tokens (we'll also break out 2k–4k).

Hyperscaler/comparator notes:
- We will run one managed hyperscaler endpoint (their public managed API) + one self-hosted hyperscaler VM if HyperAPI confirms which provider they run in prod (Anita: you mentioned two providers during the call). This will create a 3-way baseline: HyperAPI prod, hyperscaler-managed, hyperscaler-self-hosted, and Redwood.

Data collection format: JSONL traces (timestamped events) + CSV summary. We'll upload to the Drive folder in related_links.

Open question: do we include network egress variability in the baseline? That can swing p95 a lot — I recommend starting with same-region runs and then a small geo-variance sweep.

Action items (updated):
- Anita: anonymized trace + confirmation of their prod provider names + model hashes by 10/21 (owner).
- Marissa: upload runbook + k6 scripts + result dashboard template by 10/22 (owner).
- Rishi: ensure KV cache flags and batcher config are reproducible across runs (owner).

I added a short checklist to the Drive runbook (link above). Going to schedule the readout 10/27 11:00 PT — ping if different time works for you.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com


On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 09:30 AM -0700, Anita Kaur <a.kaur@hyperapi.com> wrote:

Thanks — that timeline works. We'll scrub and send a sample anonymized trace (session markers retained) this afternoon and will confirm which hyperscaler we use for the self-hosted flow. We'll also attempt a mirror run from our side and share results if time permits.

-Anita
